title: Global allocator, size, free, realloc, statistics, and alarm core

scope.rationale: These six malloc.c functions are the immediate global allocator closure beneath connection heap fallback and reallocation. They combine method-table calls, rounding, statistics, soft/hard alarms, and allocator ownership.
excluded_responsibilities: Memory status query API and limit setter API

external_source_responsibilities: Configured sqlite3_mem_methods callbacks and roundup/usable-size contracts
dependencies.caller_closure: The direct global allocation functions called by connection heap fallback are assigned. Admission remains blocked on allocator configuration/status/mutex state and alarm ordering units.

inputs: Requested byte count and optional prior heap pointer
Configured allocator method table, memory-stat mode, soft/hard limits, and current statistics
outputs: Eight-byte-aligned allocation, preserved prior pointer on failed realloc, exact usable size, and updated status highwaters/counts
contracts.ownership: xMalloc/xRealloc/xFree own heap storage. Failed realloc preserves the old pointer. Zero-size realloc frees it.
contracts.state_and_results: Maximum-allocation rejection, roundup, memory/malloc-count status, malloc-size highwater, nearly-full state, hard-limit rejection, and alarm ordering follow malloc.c.
contracts.locks_callbacks_io: STATIC_MEM mutex protects statistics. Alarm path releases it around sqlite3_release_memory and reacquires it. Configured allocator callbacks run in source order. No I/O.
contracts.failure_and_continuation: Allocator null and hard-limit failures do not corrupt statistics or old realloc ownership; later requests may continue.

representation_differences: C global mem0/config method-table state is consolidated in memory.Manager and Backend.
The pinned release-memory implementation is a no-op, and Manager preserves C's release/reacquire of the allocator mutex around the alarm call; the C/Zig event trace observes the exact handoff.
C status integer slots are represented by named Manager counters/highwaters.

oracle.protocol: The infrastructure differential installs matched exact-size allocators and instrumented mutex methods in C and Zig. It compares roundup, allocation, usable-size, alarm-time STATIC_MEM leave/reenter, hard-limit realloc rejection, free, statistics, nearly-full state, and old-byte preservation as one exact internal event trace. Existing Manager tests additionally cover zero/oversize, memory-stat-disabled, configurable backends, one-shot/sticky failures, initialization failure, and continuation.
internal_observations: allocator callback sequence and rounded sizes
oracle.normalization: Backend pointers are allocation identities; sizes, counters, result nullability, callbacks, and event order are exact.

assurance.oom: Manager tests cover one-shot/sticky allocation and realloc failures; the C/Zig trace covers hard-limit rejection with old-pointer and byte preservation.
assurance.io_crash_concurrency: No I/O. The matched configured-mutex trace proves exact STATIC_MEM release/reacquire around the no-op release-memory alarm; broader global allocator concurrency assurance remains separate.
assurance.malformed_input: Zero and excessive sizes are tested.
assurance.continuation: Failed realloc ownership and later successful allocation are tested natively.
assurance.performance: Roundup, direct backend calls, and alarm-time mutex handoff are preserved; subsystem benchmarks remain open.

integration.production_owner: src/core/memory.zig Manager candidate shared by public and connection allocation
integration.native_call_path: Public auto-initializing APIs enter global.process_coordinator; connection and VDBE heap fallbacks then call memory.processManager, which asserts that the coordinator has started the one process Manager. The former memory-only lazy-start path is removed.
integration.bounded_owner_retired: Yes for allocator lifecycle and allocation state: only global.process_coordinator starts/stops the production process Manager, and tools/verify_config.py rejects reintroduction of a memory-only lifecycle bypass. Top-level lifecycle trace promotion remains a dependency before this unit receives subsystem-integration credit.

independent_review.notes: Internal allocator callback/status/alarm traces now match. Global initialization/configuration ownership, broader concurrency/performance assurance, and independent review remain.

known_blockers: Allocator lifecycle ownership is consolidated; source-equivalent top-level initialization/refcount event evidence remains required before subsystem-integration promotion.
Complete broader concurrency/performance assurance through the final process allocator owner.
